prompt: Which workspace contains the channel where a teammate's message diagnosing the root cause of our GPU memory incident got a 🎉 reaction from someone in that channel?
binding_note: The workspace must be reached through a channel (core-infra) whose member (Priya) authored the specific root-cause diagnosis message, and that same message must carry a tada/🎉 reaction from a channel member. Priya's membership, her authorship of the diagnosis message, and a stored tada reaction on that exact message must all bind to the same records; the only stored reaction in the environment is an 'eyes' reaction on an unrelated message by a different author, so no workspace satisfies the full chain.

roles.facts: T01WORKSPACE is the only workspace; it owns core-infra, engineering, and other channels.
roles.reason: The sole visible workspace is the candidate answer, but the full route condition never resolves to it because no matching reaction exists.

roles.facts: C_INFRA ('core-infra') belongs to T01WORKSPACE; discusses infra incidents including GPU memory pressure.
roles.reason: Supplies the conversation node on the route toward the workspace.

roles.facts: U_PRIYA is a member of C_INFRA.
roles.reason: Establishes the conversation-membership binding required before the authored message can count.

roles.facts: U_PRIYA (Priya Sharma), core-infra member, authored the pprof root-cause diagnosis.
roles.reason: The user node the route must pass through between membership and message.

roles.facts: Message 1706001931 in C_INFRA by U_PRIYA: 'Got the pprof delta—it's definitely the batch size increase hitting a hard CUDA memory limit...' identifies the actual root cause; no reaction is stored on it.
roles.reason: This is the message the identifying description points to, but it carries no reaction at all, so the chain breaks here.

roles.facts: Message 1706001890 in C_INFRA by U_LUKAS discusses CUDA allocator ceilings and tensor allocation, related but not the root-cause conclusion; no reaction stored.
roles.reason: Same channel and topic area, wrong authored message for the 'diagnosis' description, and still lacks any reaction.

roles.facts: Message 1706110000.000100 in C03IJKL9012 (engineering) by U_LUKAS about circuit-tracer OOM errors; unrelated to the GPU memory-incident diagnosis in core-infra.
roles.reason: Different channel, different topic, wrong message for the described diagnosis.

roles.facts: The only stored reaction in the environment: 'eyes' on message 1706110000.000100 by U01AGENBOT9.
roles.reason: Wrong emoji (eyes, not tada) and on the wrong message entirely, so it cannot satisfy the 🎉-on-diagnosis-message condition.

obligations.name: workspace_answer
obligations.description: Identify the workspace reached via: a channel containing a member who authored the specific GPU-memory-incident root-cause diagnosis message, where that message received a tada/🎉 reaction from a channel member. No workspace satisfies this full chain because the diagnosis message carries no reaction and the only stored reaction in the system is a different emoji on an unrelated message.
obligations.scope: workspace(s) reachable through core-infra-style channels via a member's authored, reacted-to root-cause message

task_spec.text: Determine which workspace contains a channel where a member's message diagnosing the root cause of the GPU memory incident received a 🎉 reaction from a teammate; report the workspace or state that none qualifies.

access_plan: Use auth.test/users.info to confirm the acting user's visible workspace, then conversations.list (types=public_channel,private_channel) to enumerate channels including core-infra; use conversations.members on core-infra to confirm Priya's membership, and conversations.history to locate her root-cause message about the CUDA memory limit. Call reactions.get on that message's timestamp/channel to check for a tada reaction, finding none. Broaden the check to other stored reactions (only the unrelated 'eyes' reaction on a circuit-tracer message in the engineering channel) to confirm no channel/message pair in the visible workspace meets the described condition, so no workspace can be returned as a match.
